completion:
These are the records made by A and G supervisors and others as soon as possible after the workplace accident/illness occurs.
3. These records need to be printed out (even if it's just on one sheet of A4) and filed in a safe and protected place. If the incident declaration includes photos that document the damage, these should be printed out and filed as well. (General location 2)
4. At the end of the shift you need to file them properly.

If you lose an incident report i.e. the front page, the paper record and any photos the Health and Safety team will not consider them to be valid.

5. You can still use the data to assess and monitor trends within your own team, but it will not be used for company reporting.
6. Always use the Incident Form (see next page) - this is the official way to record all information regarding accidents and incidents on site.
